newsitem.title: USA: General Mills launches school program.
newsitem.headline: General Mills launches school program.

text.p: General Mills Inc on Monday announced a program to help elementary schools earn money when they turn in box tops from General Mills cereal boxes.

The Minneapols-based food giant, which holds a 24 percent share of the cereal market, used Olympic gold medal swimmer and Colorado resident Amy Van Dyken to announce the program at the school she attended.
The cereal maker already has Amy Van Dyken on its Wheaties cereal box.
"It only takes 15 minutes to eat breakfast," Van Dyken told aboaut 250 youngsters at Willow Creek school in suburban Denver.
Under the program, elementary schools will receive $0.15 for every "Big G Box Tops for Education" logo turned in up, to a $10,000 limit.

There are some 85,000 elementary schools in the United States and General Mills has already signed up 15,000 of them. Kate Curry, promotion manager, said the company expects to enroll another 5,000 to 6,000 schools in the next two weeks.
General Mills spokesman David Dix denied the campaign was an escalation of the cereal wars.

"First of all, we don't think there are cereal wars and if there are it's not between us. It's between Kellogg Co and (Philip Morris Co unit) Post (Cereal Co)," Dix said, adding that General Mills lowered its cereal prices two years before its competitors.
